locus_a: Main-article abstract (via Europe PMC, PMID 42690843): "275 alpha-branched amine-containing ionizable lipids were generated in a one-pot process from amines, aldehydes, and boronic acids"
locus_b: SI p.S5 draws 26 amines x 8 boronic acids x 14 aldehydes = 2912 possible combinations; the SI names exactly 9 members (stage00_scan_for_values.py: 9 distinct AxByCz labels across 49 pages) and nowhere states which 275 were made
why: 275 is 9.4%% of 2912 and is not any product of the panel sizes (26x8=208, 26x14=364, 8x14=112, 26+8+14=48), so the subset cannot be reconstructed by arithmetic. Enumerating 2912 would fabricate 2903 lipids that were never made; enumerating a guessed 275 would be worse. DECISIONS.md D-1.

locus_b: Four independent statements in the same SI say ESTER: (a) its own precursor on p.S8 is "6-hydroxyhexyl 4-methyloctanoate (C8i)"; (b) the 13C on p.S10 has a carbonyl at 174.4 ppm; (c) the structure drawn on p.S11 for C9/C10 and on p.S5 for C8 carries a C=O (the bond-line count 19 matches the ester, 18 would match the ether); (d) the printed HRMS calcd is for C15H29O3 ([M+H]+ 257.2111) -- the ether is C15H30O2, [M+H]+ 243.2319, 14 Da lighter
why: The ether name contradicts the oxygen count the authors themselves print. One wrong name against four concordant structural statements. The title is the error.

claim: C8i was made from nonanoic acid.
locus_a: SI p.S8: "Following the general procedure A, nonanoic acid (317.8 uL, 2.0 mmol) were used as starting material" -- under the heading 6-hydroxyhexyl 4-METHYLoctanoate (C8i)
locus_b: SI p.S8, the C9i entry immediately below, uses the identical sentence and the identical volume (317.8 uL) for nonanoic acid, which is correct there
what_we_emitted: C8 built from 4-methyloctanoic acid, per the compound name, the 13C (19.4 ppm methyl doublet carbon) and the drawn structure
why: A copy-paste from the C9i entry. 4-methyloctanoic acid and nonanoic acid are isomers (both C9H18O2), so the yield arithmetic and HRMS are unchanged and nothing internal could catch it. The compound NAME and the branch drawn on p.S5 are the evidence.

claim: The Dess-Martin oxidation of C8/C9/C10 starts from C8/C9/C10.
locus_a: SI p.S10-S11: "Following the general procedure B, C8 (258.4 mg, 1.0 mmol) were used as starting material" (and likewise C9 258.4 mg, C10 272.4 mg)
locus_b: The starting material of general procedure B is the hydroxy ester, i.e. C8i/C9i/C10i. The printed MASSES prove it: 258.4 mg / 1.0 mmol = 258.4 g/mol = the MW of C8i and C9i (258.40); 272.4 = the MW of C10i (272.42). The aldehydes themselves are 256.38 / 256.38 / 270.41
what_we_emitted: nothing -- these are intermediates, not corpus structures
why: The amounts are right and only the labels are wrong, so the chemistry is unaffected. Recorded because a reader reconstructing the route from the labels alone would start from the product.

locus_a: SI p.S11: "HRMS (ESI/Q-TOF) m/z: [M+H]+ calcd for C16H31O3, 271.2268; found, 2271.2291"
locus_b: calcd on the same line is 271.2268; a found mass of 2271 Da is impossible for a C16 ester
why: A leading-digit typo. 271.2291 is +2.3 mDa from calcd, in line with every other value in the SI.

locus_b: -41.9 mDa, -122.7 ppm. The other eight lipids in the same SI fall between -7.1 and +6.1 ppm (A18B1C1 +0.4, A18B8C14 +1.4); no Q-TOF run producing those produces -123 ppm
what_we_emitted: A2B8C1 = N1-(heptadecan-9-yl)-N3,N3-dimethylpropane-1,3-diamine, built from the calcd formula and the compound name
why: A transcription error in the FOUND value, not a structural problem: the calcd 341.3890 matches our structure to +0.03 mDa and the name, the 1H NMR integration and the drawn bond-line count (23) all agree. Flagged, not corrected -- we do not know what the instrument actually read.

locus_a: SI p.S3: "Nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR and 11B-NMR) spectra were measured on JEOL JNM-ECZ500s [500 MHz (1H), 126 MHz (13C)] and Bruker Avance III HD 300 [96 MHz (11B)]"
locus_b: No 11B spectrum appears anywhere in the 49-page SI; the spectra section (p.S34-S49) is 1H, 13C, LRMS, HRMS and one HPLC trace. The same sentence's bracket already mixes 13C into a list that says 1H and 11B
why: Cosmetic, recorded because a reader looking for boron speciation evidence (which would bear on the radical mechanism) will not find it.
